transcript.text: theres a funny smell from my oven when its on

A 'funny' smell when an oven first turns on can be normal if it's a new appliance (manufacturing oils burning off), but given your description, we need to rule out a serious electrical fault first. The most critical possibility is overheating at the mains connection point (the terminal block) where the cable enters the back of the oven. This happens due to loose connections or high resistance and can be a fire hazard. Please do this check now:
1. Switch off the oven and isolate it at the wall switch or consumer unit.
2. Carefully look at the back of the oven, specifically where the thick mains cable enters the appliance casing.
3. Check for any signs of melting plastic, charring (blackened/burnt marks), discolouration, or a white powdery residue on the connection point. If you see ANY of these signs, STOP using the oven immediately and do not turn it back on until a qualified engineer has inspected it. If the area looks clean and normal, tell me exactly what the smell resembles (e.g., burnt dust, plastic, food) and whether this is a new or old appliance.

I can't see the back, the cooker's too heavy to pull out on my own. It's an old one, about 12 years. The smell is more like hot plastic or electrical, seems to come from behind or underneath, not inside the oven. The cooker switch looks a bit brown at one corner and felt warm too.

⚠ Stop using this appliance
A burning or hot-plastic smell, smoke, scorching or melting can mean an electrical fault or a fire risk. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it (or turn it off at the fuse box), and don't run it again — not even as a test — until it has been checked by a qualified engineer. The brown discoloration and warmth on the cooker switch, combined with a smell of hot plastic or electrical burning coming from behind/underneath, strongly indicates an overheating fault at the main power connection. This is almost probably caused by a loose or corroded terminal block inside the oven where the mains cable connects, or a failing switch mechanism. This is a serious fire hazard. The heat and smell you are describing are classic signs of high resistance at the electrical connection point. As this involves the fixed mains supply and internal wiring, it is unsafe to attempt any repair yourself. Please stop using the oven immediately. Do not turn it back on again until a qualified engineer has inspected and repaired the fault.
